external_entities.name: calling service
external_entities.description: A backend operated by another team that calls the inference gateway.
external_entities.source_excerpt: Other teams' backends call our inference gateway

external_entities.name: calling team's users
external_entities.description: Users whose typed content may be carried in prompts sent by calling teams.
external_entities.source_excerpt: raw prompts, which sometimes carry whatever the calling team's users typed

external_entities.name: ML engineer
external_entities.description: An engineer who publishes new model artifacts to the registry bucket.
external_entities.source_excerpt: ML engineers publish new model artifacts to the registry bucket
external_entities.notes: The source is uncertain about what governs who can push and says it may be a shared group account: "I'm not sure what governs who can push — I think it is a shared group account."

processes.name: inference gateway
processes.description: A FastAPI service on GKE exposed on the internet that receives inference requests and forwards them to the model server, while logging requests and responses.
processes.source_excerpt: our inference gateway, a FastAPI service on GKE that we expose on the internet
processes.notes: API keys are issued per calling team and have never been expired.

processes.name: model server
processes.description: The service that runs the actual model on GPU nodes in the model network.
processes.source_excerpt: the model server, which runs the actual model on GPU nodes in our model network
processes.notes: The source says the model network is meant to be reachable only from the gateway.

data_stores.name: model registry bucket
data_stores.description: A bucket from which the model server loads model artifacts at startup and to which ML engineers publish new artifacts.
data_stores.source_excerpt: model artifacts from a model registry bucket
data_stores.notes: The source says: "I don't believe anything verifies the artifact hasn't been swapped — we just trust the bucket."

data_stores.name: Redis feature store
data_stores.description: A Redis store containing customer features such as account age and spend bands per customer.
data_stores.source_excerpt: a Redis feature store on the same network
data_stores.notes: Redis has no password and is only reachable inside the model network.

data_stores.name: inference log
data_stores.description: A BigQuery log containing every request and response for debugging, including raw prompts.
data_stores.source_excerpt: the gateway writes every request and response into an inference log in BigQuery
data_stores.notes: Raw prompts sometimes carry whatever the calling team's users typed.

data_flows.name: inference requests
data_flows.description: Inference requests sent by a calling service to the inference gateway.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Other teams' backends call our inference gateway
data_flows.notes: Callers pass an API key in a header. Keys are issued per calling team and have never been expired.

data_flows.name: forwarded inference request
data_flows.description: The inference gateway forwards requests to the model server.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The gateway forwards the request to the model server

data_flows.name: model artifact load
data_flows.description: The model server loads model artifacts from the model registry bucket at startup.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The model server loads model artifacts from a model registry bucket at startup
data_flows.notes: The model server uses its own service account for this.

data_flows.name: customer feature read
data_flows.description: The model server reads customer features from the Redis feature store.
data_flows.source_excerpt: the model server reads from a Redis feature store on the same network
data_flows.data_description: Customer features including account age and spend bands per customer

data_flows.name: inference request and response log
data_flows.description: The inference gateway writes every request and response to the inference log for debugging.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The gateway writes every request and response into an inference log in BigQuery, for debugging
data_flows.notes: The logged data includes raw prompts, which sometimes carry whatever the calling team's users typed.
data_flows.data_description: Every inference request and response, including raw prompts

data_flows.name: model artifact publish
data_flows.description: ML engineers publish new model artifacts to the registry bucket.
data_flows.source_excerpt: ML engineers publish new model artifacts to the registry bucket
data_flows.notes: The source is uncertain about the push authorization and says it may be a shared group account: "I'm not sure what governs who can push — I think it is a shared group account."

trust_boundaries.name: cloud
trust_boundaries.description: The cloud-hosted environment containing the inference gateway and cloud data stores, along with the other teams' cloud-hosted calling services and ML engineers' access context.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: two of the calling services are in a different cloud

trust_boundaries.name: model network
trust_boundaries.description: The network containing the model server and Redis feature store, intended to be reachable only from the inference gateway.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: the model network is meant to be reachable only from the gateway

assumptions.assumption: The inference gateway presents a web interface because it is described as a FastAPI service.
assumptions.basis: FastAPI is an HTTP application framework, and the source describes the component as a FastAPI service.

assumptions.assumption: The model server is internal-facing rather than internet-facing.
assumptions.basis: The source says the model network is meant to be reachable only from the inference gateway.

assumptions.assumption: The Redis feature store contains confidential data.
assumptions.basis: The source states that it contains account age and spend bands per customer, which are customer-related data whose disclosure may harm a person or the business.
